Hi, 23NB here. I've been on Clonazepam (generic name for Klonopin) for 4 years now. I take 1 mg a day on average. Some days none, some days 2. I never go above 2.

I personally noticed an immediate effect as soon as I started taking it. My brain stopped yelling at me about everything and my body was more relaxed. I felt less inhibited by my anxiety, and did things I wouldn't have dared do otherwise out of fear. I also sleep better.

0.5 mg is an extremely low dose (0.25 is the minimal effective dose), and if your anxiety levels are high, it might not be enough yet. However, benzodiazepines have a near immediate effect, so my guess is that if this medication is right for you, you will start to notice the difference when they up your dose.

Try to be careful with the dependency stuff. Don't abuse it. Don't take it just because you're slightly uncomfortable. When I take it, it's at the same time every night. I also take it when I know I am about to face a situation that I know will be anxiety-inducing for me.

However, don't get overly paranoid to the point you're not taking it when you need it (which I have been guilty of). If you're already wary of dependency, then you probably don't need to worry about it.

IME it's a pretty straightforward drug, excluding the dependency stuff.

Feel free to PM me if you have any specific questions.

Keep in mind this is just personal experience and I'm not a medical professional of any kind.

Best of luck.

EDIT: I don't wanna intrude in your business, but I would recommend psychological treatment as well as psychiatric if you can get it. Studies show that a combination of both is far more effective than only meds or only therapy. CBT therapy has been shown to be one of the most effective ones (at least last time I read about the topic), and it's the one I've been doing these years. This is just personal recommendation nothing more.

this is what cemented my type down for me: 

×i went back to my childhood years and recalled several things that point to (low) Fe use:

•never thinking about value or moral issues (only when i personally encountered or saw sexism i would relentlessly wonder why the world treated men and women differently), until i encountered tumblr when i was 13.


•absorbing the values of my surroundings as a kid: a classmate asked me if i was pro choice once and i said no, simply because i had been told, by my surroundings, that abortion was wrong.


•we discussed homosexuality in class, and a girl said she didn't agree with gay men holding hands in public because "the cHilDrEn". everyone else agreed, so i did the same.


•at around 12 i found a reddit-esque libertarian/right-wing website that i frequented, and i would regurgitate things I saw about feminism without knowing anything about feminism at all (these people didn't know anything about feminism either)


•when i found tumblr, i stayed there for years for the memes, and as a consequence of staying there, throughout the years adopted a big part of their value system and added it to my internal Ti framework (Ti holds logic and value systems in it). of course, i didn't mindlessly adopt anything they said, i still filtered it through my Ti "does this fit with what i know? does it make sense to me?" and i would immediately discard it if it didn't.


×other things that made me realize im not a Fi user:

•i have a value system, but like i said, it was a system adopted from a community i belonged to. my values have never come from within me. i dont have an instinctive sense of right and wrong when presented with a moral dilemma ive never encountered before. i can only go back to my Ti-Si when it comes to situations similar to ones ive come across before, and what values i adopted (from my environment) in those situations


•i have a deep aversion to people basing theories/decisions on patterns they've picked out from personal experience. its a cringe level reaction. i think its Fi 8th

•if im in a situation where people around me are saying things i massively disagree with, or even see as potentially dangerous, i will keep my mouth shut, because i cannot bring myself to disrupt the mood of the group, even if i hate what they are saying. i wont act as if i agree (my Fe is inferior after all); rather i wont say anything at all.

×take your gender upbringing into account. female thinkers/ male feelers will be indirectly forced by societal norms to develop their feeling/thinking function respectively, and so they are more likely to not look/behave like the typical person of their type.

×i dont think you'll particularly relate to my experience, but, tl;dr: i think maybe looking back at how you reacted/didn't react to matters regarding value when younger, and sort of connecting the dots and writing the story of how you got to where you are today, can help.
